findings.title: 4-dimension vs 9-dimension type system gap
findings.description: Reader Simulation uses QualityDimension enum (4 dims: plot, character, style, pacing) while Writing Craft Analysis uses WritingCraftDimension (9 dims: structure, character, suspense, emotion, dialogue, webnovel, hook, cliffhanger, show_tell). These two type systems are completely disconnected. No bridge exists. The DimensionAnalyzer only understands 4 dimensions. To integrate, either: (1) expand QualityDimension to 9, or (2) create a bridge that maps WritingCraftDimension results into the reader consensus flow. Option 2 is less disruptive.
findings.recommendation: Implement a WritingCraftBridge class that delegates 9-dimension analysis to writing-craft analyzers and transforms results into DimensionScore[] format consumable by ConsensusEngine. This avoids changing the core QualityDimension enum and minimizes downstream impact.

findings.title: Persona parameters mismatch between frontend and backend
findings.description: Frontend PersonaWeights (desktop/src/components/reader/PersonaSelector.tsx:9) has 4 fields: plot, character, style, pacing. Backend ReaderPersona.parameters (src-ts/reader/PersonaDefinition.ts:18) has 7 fields including toleranceThreshold, focusAreas, biases. The frontend does not expose toleranceThreshold or focusAreas editing. For R-M26-001, new fields (age, culture, readingPreference, genrePreference) need to be added to both frontend and backend types consistently.
findings.recommendation: Define a shared PersonaParameters interface in a common types package, or at minimum ensure frontend PersonaWeights extends to match backend parameters. Add new demographic fields to both.

findings.title: Anti-AI-flavor detection: no unified detector exists
findings.description: Three independent analyzers exist for style detection (StyleSystem with 30-dim vector, VoiceFingerprint, ShowTellAnalyzer with SensoryCoverage), but no unified AntiAIFlavorDetector composes them. Each analyzer operates independently. R-M26-003 requires detecting: (1) templated expressions, (2) style fingerprint drift, (3) sensory coverage insufficiency. The building blocks exist but need composition.
findings.recommendation: Create a new AntiAIFlavorAnalyzer class that composes StyleVector drift detection, SensoryCoverage threshold checking, and VoiceFingerprint consistency. Add a new 'anti_ai_flavor' AnalysisModule.

findings.title: ConsensusEngine does not support persona set partitioning
findings.description: ConsensusEngine.buildConsensus() aggregates all reactions into a single report. For A/B testing (R-M26-005), reactions need to be partitioned into two groups before consensus building, then results compared. No partitioning logic exists. The OverlayBridge also lacks marker types for group comparison.
findings.recommendation: Add buildConsensus overload accepting groupA and groupB reaction arrays. Add new OverlayMarker types ('groupA', 'groupB', 'difference'). Create new endpoint rsComparePersonasEndpoint.

findings.title: In-memory persona storage not persistent
findings.description: reader-endpoints.ts uses customPersonaStore = new Map<string, ReaderPersona>() (line 49). Custom personas are lost on restart. For production use with expanded personas (R-M26-001), persistence is needed. Similarly, analysisResultCache (line 50) is in-memory.
findings.recommendation: Replace in-memory Map with KnowledgeMemoryEngineAdapter or file-based persistence. The personalization-service.ts already uses this pattern (line 40).

findings.title: RevisionServiceImpl writerFn is a no-op
findings.description: In RevisionServiceImpl.revise() (src-ts/services/revision-service.ts:87-97), the writerFn returns draft unchanged with comment '// Writer function — returns draft unchanged (actual revision happens via suggestions)'. For R-M26-004 de-AI transformation, an actual writer implementation is needed.
findings.recommendation: Implement writerFn that calls a de-AI transformation service (e.g., via LLM with de-AI system prompt, or rule-based transformation). The existing writing-helper endpoint (src-ts/mcp/endpoints/writing.ts) has detectionEvasion guard pattern that can be adapted.

findings.title: Dual i18n systems require synchronized updates
findings.description: The codebase has two i18n systems: (1) i18next with zh-CN.json/en-US.json, and (2) legacy translations.ts with 11 modular modules. New reader simulation translations need to be added to both. Risk of key mismatch between systems.
findings.recommendation: Add a new 'reader' module to translations.ts. Ensure keys are mirrored in zh-CN.json. Consider migrating legacy system to i18next-only to reduce maintenance burden.

findings.title: Fictional Dream Engine not connected to Reader Simulation
findings.description: The Fictional Dream Engine (4 layers: sympathy -> identification -> empathy -> immersion) has ImmersionCatalyst and EmpathyDeepener classes that produce immersion scores. These are not connected to the Reader Simulation's 4 dimensions. The 'emotion' dimension from WritingCraftDimension could be enriched with immersion data.
findings.recommendation: Optional enhancement: connect ImmersionCatalyst output to the emotion/suspense dimension scoring in the reader engine. This would provide deeper emotional analysis than heuristic scoring.

findings.title: Reader simulation module has test coverage gaps
findings.description: From the test coverage analysis (20260616-analyze-test-coverage), the narrative/ directory has 93% coverage but fictional_dream/identification.ts is listed as uncovered. The reader/ module tests were not explicitly found in the coverage report, suggesting potential gaps.
findings.recommendation: Verify test coverage for reader/ module before implementing R-M26 changes. Add tests for new functionality (persona expansion, 9-dimension bridge, A/B comparison, anti-AI detection).

findings.title: Existing detectionEvasion guard can be extended for anti-AI
findings.description: writing-endpoints.ts (line 351) has a detectionEvasion flag that changes the system prompt to 'avoid AI-generated typical patterns'. This is a primitive form of anti-AI-flavor detection. R-M26-003 can build on this by making the detection systematic and score-based rather than just a prompt toggle.
findings.recommendation: Extract the detectionEvasion concept into a proper AntiAIFlavorDetector service with scoring, then use the score to drive the writing helper's system prompt intensity.

risks.title: Type system cascade: QualityDimension enum expansion breaks downstream consumers
risks.description: QualityDimension is a hardcoded enum used in HardConstraintViolation, HardConstraintResult, DimensionAnalyzer, ConsensusEngine, OverlayBridge, and all frontend components. Expanding from 4 to 9 dimensions would require changes across 15+ files. Missing any consumer would cause type errors or runtime failures.
risks.mitigation: Use the bridge approach (F-001 recommendation) instead of expanding the enum. Create a WritingCraftBridge that maps 9-dimension results into the existing 4-dimension consensus flow, or add a parallel 9-dimension flow that coexists with the legacy 4-dimension flow. Deprecate 4-dimension flow gradually.

risks.title: Frontend-backend type drift during persona expansion
risks.description: The frontend PersonaSelector and backend PersonaDefinition types are already partially mismatched (4 vs 7 fields). Adding 4 more fields (age, culture, readingPreference, genrePreference) increases the risk of frontend-backend contract drift. API serialization/deserialization errors could occur if fields are added inconsistently.
risks.mitigation: Create a shared PersonaParameters type in a common package (or src-ts/types/reader.ts with frontend re-export). Use strict validation in the rsCreateCustomPersonaEndpoint. Add contract tests for persona serialization.

risks.title: Anti-AI-flavor detection accuracy: false positives on human-written text
risks.description: Anti-AI-flavor detection based on style fingerprinting, sensory coverage, and template patterns risks false positives on human-written text that happens to have low sensory coverage or matches common patterns. This could alienate users if their human-written text is flagged as 'AI-flavored'.
risks.mitigation: (1) Use ensemble scoring (combine multiple signals with weights, not single threshold). (2) Provide confidence scores, not binary flags. (3) Allow user calibration/baseline extraction from their own writing samples. (4) Include human-written reference corpus for comparison.

risks.title: De-AI transformation quality: over-correction destroying author voice
risks.description: Aggressive de-AI transformation could over-correct and destroy the author's natural voice, making text worse rather than better. The transformation needs to preserve author style while removing AI artifacts.
risks.mitigation: (1) Extract author baseline style fingerprint before transformation. (2) Use delta scoring: measure distance from baseline, not just AI-flavor score. (3) Make transformation intensity configurable. (4) Provide before/after comparison UI. (5) Allow user to accept/reject per-suggestion.

risks.title: A/B testing performance: doubling analysis cost
risks.description: A/B comparison requires running the full analysis pipeline twice (once per persona group). If each analysis is LLM-powered, this doubles API cost and latency. The current in-memory cache (analysisResultCache) does not help since groups are different.
risks.mitigation: (1) Cache per-persona results, then combine for consensus. (2) Use lightweight heuristic analysis for initial A/B, with LLM only on disagreement. (3) Add progress streaming for long-running A/B comparisons. (4) Consider parallel execution with Promise.all.

risks.title: i18n key explosion: maintaining two translation systems
risks.description: Adding reader simulation translations to both i18next (JSON) and legacy (TypeScript modules) systems doubles maintenance. Risk of key drift and missing translations in one system.
risks.mitigation: (1) Add reader module only to legacy system first (lower risk). (2) Run ensureTranslationShape() validation. (3) Plan migration to i18next-only in future phase. (4) Use automated key extraction from source code.

risks.title: In-memory storage limits scalability
risks.description: customPersonaStore and analysisResultCache are in-memory Maps. As personas expand (R-M26-001) and analysis dimensions increase (R-M26-002), memory usage grows. No eviction policy exists.
risks.mitigation: (1) Add LRU eviction to caches. (2) Persist personas to disk/knowledge store. (3) Add cache size limits and monitoring.
